The problem

Growth takes more than scattered tools.

The merchants this is built for are not short of software. They are short of software that talks to itself.

Six tools that do not connect

A store here, an ads account there, a courier portal, a spreadsheet for returns. The joins are a person, and that person is the founder.

Cash on delivery leaks margin

In Egypt and Saudi, a refused parcel costs the shipping both ways. Confirmation before dispatch is the difference between a good month and a flat one.

Agencies bill whether it works or not

A monthly retainer detached from the outcome, and no visibility into what the spend actually bought.

The product

One platform. Every channel.

Set it up once, and the parts that used to need a person run themselves.

AI that finds the demand

Product and customer recommendations, campaign generation, and a set of skills that optimise against what actually sold rather than against impressions.

Confirmation before dispatch

Every cash-on-delivery order confirmed on WhatsApp, follow-ups automatic, the silent ones surfaced as a call list. The single clearest margin win in the region.

Shipping that is wired in

Egypt Post and Bosta integrated for labels, pickups and tracking — plus a carrier app approved and listed in the Shopify App Store.

Collection that closes the loop

InstaPay payment links and reconciliation, so the money arriving is matched to the order that earned it.

How it works

Why this is a platform and not an agency.

An agency sells hours. This sells a system that keeps working when nobody is watching it.

  1. 01

    Connect the store

    Shopify today, with the integration surface built to take the next platform without a rewrite.

  2. 02

    Import the catalogue

    Products, variants and the weights that make shipping accurate rather than approximate.

  3. 03

    Turn on confirmation

    WhatsApp flows go live before the first order, not bolted on after the returns start.

  4. 04

    Wire the carriers

    Labels, pickups and tracking from inside the order, so nobody opens a courier portal.

  5. 05

    Let the AI run

    Recommendations, campaigns and creative generated against the catalogue and the sales history.

  6. 06

    Watch one screen

    Revenue, orders, spend, returns and delivery state in a single view instead of six tabs.

The model

Flat rate. No surprises.

Priced so a merchant can predict it, and so the incentive is retention rather than billable hours.

Monthly subscription

A flat fee per merchant. No percentage of spend, no percentage of revenue, no line item that grows when they succeed.

Multi-tenant from the start

Every merchant is an isolated tenant on shared infrastructure — the reason the marginal cost of the next customer is small.

Two markets, one engine

Egypt and Saudi differ in carrier, currency and payment rail, not in product. The same platform serves both.

Managed tier on top

For merchants who want it done rather than run: the same platform with an operator behind it, at a higher monthly rate.

The ask

What the money is for.

The build is behind us. What is missing is distribution.

  • Merchant acquisitionA repeatable way to reach cash-on-delivery merchants in Egypt and Saudi, measured on cost per paying merchant.
  • Carrier and gateway coverageEach new carrier or payment rail widens the addressable market. They are integrations, and integrations are schedulable.
  • A commercial vehicle in SaudiA registration and a bank account a Saudi gateway will settle into. It is the gate in front of the second market.
  • An operator, not an engineerSomeone to run merchant success while the platform keeps being built. The scarce resource here has never been code.
